newsitem.title: YEMEN: French hostage in Yemen freed unharmed.
newsitem.headline: French hostage in Yemen freed unharmed.

text.p: A French diplomat, kidnapped by a leading tribe six days ago, was freed early on Sunday, an interior ministry official told the official news agency SABA.

"The diplomat was released unharmed and has returned safely to his home after police forces succeeded in freeing him from the hands of the elements of sabotage that abducted him," added the unnamed official.
Yemen will not tolerate "tampering with the country's stability and security and will firmly deal with outlaws".
He gave no further details. The French embassy and other officials were not available for comment.
The captors, members of al-Toaiman tribe, released their hostage late on Saturday to three prominent tribal chiefs who were mediating on behalf of the government, a local official said.

The diplomat, said by Yemeni authorities to be a first secretary at the embassy, was held in Marib province, 170 km (100 miles) north of the Yemeni capital after being seized as he drove in Sanaa on Monday.
The kidnappers had dropped their demands earlier and asked for a guarantee they would not be prosecuted if they release their hostage.
It was not immediately clear what arrangements were reached by the negotiators.

The Toaiman tribe demanded government compensation for losses to homes, farms, water pumps and wells by floods that killed 65 people in June. It also wants more jobs and the settlement of a land dispute.

In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or foreigners as bargaining chips. At least two diplomats, an American and a Saudi ambassador, have been among the kidnap victims.
The demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.
